plan.headline: Lotus Tile & Stone: 14 entries reviewed, with $123,460 in IEEPA duties paid. One entry ($6,780) is due today, Oct 24, 2026.

steps.title: Today: claim entry HP7-0414106-2 in CAPE
steps.detail: This entry appears eligible for a $6,780 refund through CAPE (CBP's refund claim system), but its deadline is today, Oct 24, 2026. Call your broker right away and ask them to file it.

steps.title: Claim entry HP7-0414117-9 in CAPE
steps.detail: This entry appears eligible for a $3,750 refund through CAPE. File by Nov 8, 2026.

steps.title: Claim entry HP7-0414533-5 in CAPE
steps.detail: This entry appears eligible for a $13,230 refund through CAPE. File by Nov 16, 2026.

steps.title: File a protest for entry HP7-0413540-6
steps.detail: This entry was finalized (liquidated) too long ago for CAPE, so it needs a protest, which is a formal request to CBP to correct the entry. It appears eligible for $3,640, and the protest window closes Nov 22, 2026.

steps.title: Fix entry HP7-0414879-0, then claim it in CAPE
steps.detail: The goods value is reported on the wrong line (an IEEPA Chapter 99 line), and CAPE rejects the entry until your broker moves it to the Chapter 1-97 line. Once fixed, it appears eligible for $4,460. Aim to finish by Nov 30, 2026.

steps.title: File a protest for entry HP7-0413822-4
steps.detail: This entry is also too far past finalization for CAPE, so it needs a protest. It appears eligible for $15,840, and the protest window closes Dec 12, 2026.

steps.title: Claim entry HP7-0415250-8 in CAPE
steps.detail: This entry appears eligible for a $3,880 refund through CAPE. File by Dec 21, 2026.

steps.title: Claim three more entries in CAPE (no deadline given)
steps.detail: These appear eligible: HP7-0419921-5 ($50,000), HP7-0415702-7 ($7,740) and HP7-0416475-1 ($3,180). The $50,000 and $3,180 amounts come only from your statement, so ask your broker to confirm them against the entry records.

steps.title: Claim two court-plaintiff entries in CAPE Phase 3
steps.detail: Because you are a plaintiff in the Court of International Trade (CIT) case and gave CBP your importer number by July 30, 2026, these appear eligible under CAPE Phase 3, which opened Oct 6, 2026: HP7-0412207-3 ($4,125) and HP7-0412988-1 ($2,860).

steps.title: Ask your broker about entry HP7-0416018-4
steps.detail: A surety (the bond company) paid the IEEPA duties on this $3,975 entry, and CBP says not to file it in CAPE. Your broker can tell you what other route, if any, applies.

steps.title: Nothing to do on entry HP7-0411873-2
steps.detail: No IEEPA duty was paid on this entry, so there is nothing to refund. Section 301 and 232 duties are not part of this refund.

plan.broker_email_subject: Urgent: IEEPA refund filings for Lotus Tile & Stone, with one entry due today
plan.broker_email_body:
Hi,

I reviewed our IEEPA refund options as of Oct 24, 2026. Could you please confirm and handle the following? I know this isn't legal advice, so I'd like your read on each item.

URGENT, due today (Oct 24, 2026):
- File CAPE for HP7-0414106-2 ($6,780).

CAPE filings with upcoming deadlines:
- HP7-0414117-9 ($3,750), due Nov 8, 2026
- HP7-0414533-5 ($13,230), due Nov 16, 2026
- HP7-0415250-8 ($3,880), due Dec 21, 2026

Protests (too long since liquidation for CAPE):
- HP7-0413540-6 ($3,640), window closes Nov 22, 2026
- HP7-0413822-4 ($15,840), window closes Dec 12, 2026

Fix first, then CAPE:
- HP7-0414879-0 ($4,460): the goods value is on an IEEPA Chapter 99 line. Can you move it to the Chapter 1-97 line so CAPE accepts it? Target is Nov 30, 2026.

More CAPE filings (no deadline listed):
- HP7-0419921-5 ($50,000) and HP7-0416475-1 ($3,180). These amounts come only from our statement, so please verify them against the entry records.
- HP7-0415702-7 ($7,740)

CAPE Phase 3 (we are a CIT plaintiff and gave CBP our importer number by July 30, 2026):
- HP7-0412207-3 ($4,125)
- HP7-0412988-1 ($2,860)

Question on a surety entry:
- HP7-0416018-4 ($3,975): a surety paid the IEEPA duties, and CBP says not to file CAPE. What are our options?

Please let me know what you need from me and when you can file.

Thank you,
Lotus Tile & Stone LLC

issues.detail: The extraction gives stated_ieepa 3180 but lists no Chapter 99 lines. No 7501 exists for this entry, so the 3,180 comes only from the broker statement. It is unsupported by line detail, and the 9903.01/.02 subheading is unknown. Treat it as unverified.

The extraction lists no Chapter 99 line, even though the statement footnote names 9903.02.20 at 50,000.00. No 7501 exists to confirm it. The footnote shows total duty 52,400, which is about 95% IEEPA, so the figure needs verification against the entry. It appears only in a footnote, not in the main table.
issues.quote: Not shown above: entry HP7-0419921-5 (type 01, entered 03/03/2026), Open, total duty 52,400.00, IEEPA (9903.02.20) 50,000.00.

checker.summary: I checked all 14 entries against the 12 CBP 7501 pages and the broker statement. The liquidation statuses and dates match, including the reliquidated date of 08/20/2026 for HP7-0414117-9. The Chapter 99 lines and amounts match the 7501s, and the statement's IEEPA totals agree with the line detail for every entry that has a 7501. The 9903.88.xx lines are labeled as Section 301, which is correct. The surety-paid flag on HP7-0416018-4 is supported. Two entries, HP7-0416475-1 and HP7-0419921-5, have no 7501. Their IEEPA amounts rest only on the statement, and the extraction has no Chapter 99 lines for either one.

reader_notes: HP7-0414117-9: the statement row shows a liquidation date of 08/04/2026. A note below it says it was reliquidated and the corrected date is 08/20/2026 per ACE, which supersedes 08/04/2026. 2026-08-20 was recorded; check this in ACE.

HP7-0416018-4: the surety-paid note ('Duties incl. IEEPA paid by surety after missed ACH; surety claim open') sits right below this entry's row. It was assigned to this entry because of where it appears; the note does not repeat the entry number.
HP7-0416475-1: this entry appears only on the broker statement. The note says the '7501 copy not yet sent to client', so no line or HTS details are available and lines is left empty.

HP7-0419921-5: this entry appears only in a footnote on the broker statement (total duty 52,400.00, IEEPA under 9903.02.20 of 50,000.00). There is no 7501, so lines is left empty. This IEEPA amount is much larger than the others and should be checked against the actual 7501.
HP7-0411873-2: the statement shows IEEPA 0.00. Its 7501 shows only 6802.93.0010 and 9903.88.15.
No document mentions protests, drawback, reconciliation flags or AD/CVD for any entry, so those flags are all false.
Most 7501s show no entered value on the Chapter 99 rows, so those are null. Only HP7-0414879-0's 9903.02.69 row shows an entered value (22,300.00).
